# 1. Executive Snapshot

- **Durable execution just got a $12.55B price tag.** Temporal raised $550M (Series E, led by Lightspeed): run rate above $250M, growing over 200% year over year, 4,300+ paying customers including OpenAI, Nvidia, Netflix and JPMorgan. This is the third straight day of "agents must survive failure" signals, and the first with hard revenue behind it.
- **Databases are being rebuilt for agents.** Supabase raised $150M (GIC) and announced it is acquiring Turso (libSQL/SQLite in Rust). Supabase says over 1M databases are created weekly and about 70% come from agents or AI tools. If we build on Supabase, expect database-per-agent patterns and product changes. Deal price and closing are undisclosed.
- **Always-on agents are now table stakes across vendors.** OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse and Anthropic's reply (Cowork folded into Claude, scheduled jobs that run with the laptop closed; Claude Code routines in research preview) all do the same thing. The decision is no longer whether to use unattended agents but what credentials they hold.
- **Agent tools are becoming programmable.** Claude Code "mods" (TypeScript hooks around tool calls, permission requests and prompts, shipped Oct 1-2) let us enforce policy in the tool itself, which fits the allowlist work from yesterday.
- **Recommended attention level: Medium.** No new emergency. Finish the Plugin4Shell controls, then decide how we will run unattended agents.

# 2. Technologies Worth Watching

**Technology:** Durable execution (Temporal) as agent infrastructure

**Category:** Cloud & Infrastructure / Automation

**What happened?**
Temporal raised $550M at a $12.55B valuation, more than double its valuation earlier this year. Its software lets long tasks resume after failures instead of restarting. Customers include OpenAI, Nvidia, Netflix and JPMorgan.

**Why it matters?**
Yesterday we saw two open-source harnesses (Pi Durable, Restate) add durability. A company with $250M run rate growing 200% shows buyers are paying for it in production. Long agent runs fail partway; without durable state they lose work or repeat side effects (double emails, double charges).

**Business Value:** Fewer lost or duplicated agent tasks; reliable long workflows (onboarding, billing, report generation).

**Company Relevance:** 60

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Observe (adopt only when we run a multi-step agent or workflow in production that has side effects)

**Expected Impact:** Medium

---

**Technology:** Database-per-agent architecture (Supabase + Turso)

**Category:** Cloud & Infrastructure / Data

**What happened?**
Supabase announced a $150M round and the intent to acquire Turso. Supabase cites 1M+ databases created per week, ~70% by agents or AI tools. Separately, OrioleDB (a Postgres storage engine) entered public beta on Pro, Team and Enterprise plans on Oct 1.

**Why it matters?**
Agents create throwaway, isolated databases for tasks. Isolation is a security benefit (an agent can only touch its own data) and a cost risk (database sprawl). It also signals that Supabase is consolidating the stack we may already depend on.

**Business Value:** Safer sandboxes for agent work; simpler preview and test data.

**Company Relevance:** 58 (higher if we are on Supabase)

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Observe (watch the closing terms and roadmap; no migration)

**Expected Impact:** Medium

---

**Technology:** Programmable agent harness (Claude Code mods)

**Category:** Developer Tools / Security

**What happened?**
Anthropic shipped "mods": small TypeScript functions that run before, after or in place of events such as tool calls, permission requests, prompt submission and UI rendering, in the CLI and desktop app.

**Why it matters?**
It gives us a place to enforce rules such as "block installs from non-allowlisted plugins" or "never read .env". Policy that lives in the tool beats policy that lives in a wiki. The risk is that mods are also code, so they need the same review as plugins.

**Business Value:** Enforceable guardrails and audit logging for agent use without waiting for vendor features.

**Company Relevance:** 70

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Pilot (one policy mod, reviewed and version-controlled)

**Expected Impact:** Short

# 3. New Tools & Platforms

**Tool:** Claude Code mods

**Category:** Engineering / Operations

**What does it do?**
Lets a team add TypeScript hooks that intercept agent events (tool calls, permissions, prompts) and change behavior or UI.

**Who should use it?**
Technical leads responsible for agent safety and consistent team setup.

**Business Use Case:** Block risky commands, log agent actions, enforce the plugin allowlist.

**Estimated ROI:** Medium-High if it replaces manual policing; low if nobody maintains it.

**Recommended Experiment:** Write one mod that blocks plugin installs not on our allowlist and logs every denied attempt. Keep it in the repo with code review.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 0.5-1 day

---

**Tool:** Claude Code routines (research preview)

**Category:** Automation

**What does it do?**
Runs a saved prompt plus repos and connectors unattended on a schedule, via web call, or on a GitHub event, as a cloud session.

**Who should use it?**
Teams with recurring read-heavy work: reports, dependency checks, triage.

**Business Use Case:** Recurring research and hygiene tasks without a developer present (this brief is one example).

**Estimated ROI:** Medium; research-preview terms and limits may change.

**Recommended Experiment:** Move one weekly chore (dependency or changelog review) to a routine, read-only access, output as a commit to a docs repo.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 2 hours

**Tool:** Temporal (open-source core and cloud)

**Category:** Operations / Automation

**What does it do?**
Runs workflows as code that survive crashes, retries and restarts.

**Who should use it?**
Teams with multi-step processes that touch payments, email or external APIs.

**Business Use Case:** Reliable background jobs and agent pipelines.

**Estimated ROI:** Low now; High once a failing multi-step job costs us money.

**Recommended Experiment:** Read-only: write down our one most failure-prone multi-step process and what a restart would do to it. No install.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 2 hours

# 4. Global Technology Direction

**Where is the market moving?**

1. **Agents are becoming infrastructure workloads, not chat features.** Money is flowing to the layers underneath them: workflow durability (Temporal, $12.55B), per-agent databases (Supabase/Turso), model serving (Together AI reportedly $800M at $8.3B), and open-weight models (Arcee reportedly $150M at $1B+). Dates for the last two rounds were not confirmed.
2. **The three big labs converged on the same product.** OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse and Anthropic's Claude/Cowork all offer always-on agents. Differentiation will move to price, security behavior and integrations, not the existence of the feature.
3. **Control is moving into the tool.** Anthropic's mods and OpenAI's Decisions API (cheap, low-latency decisions) show vendors exposing hooks so customers can govern agents themselves.
4. **Talent is the bottleneck.** Anthropic's $100M Claude Frontier Academy (10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by end of 2027) implies vendors see deployment skill, not model access, as the scarce resource.

**What This Means For Our Company**

- We do not need to buy an always-on agent product this quarter; we need a policy for what an unattended agent may touch.
- Our scarce resource is likely deployment skill too. Assign one named owner for agent tooling instead of letting it spread informally.
- Build workflows so state can be resumed (idempotent steps, stored progress) even if we do not adopt Temporal.
